content.comment_body: Hello everyone. I have a question: is there a way to restrict the input value for a counter? Specifically, can you set the value from either the web interface or the controller display, rather than relying on the esc+< or esc+> buttons as shown in the screenshot? For instance, if the counter should only accept values between 5 and 20, is it possible to block any value outside this range? One approach is to reset if the value exceeds the limits, but that only restores the initial value, not the minimum or maximum allowed. [user_name]
Hello [user_name], this topic was recently discussed in the German section of the forum (see [url]). Best regards [user_name] (translated with Google)
However, the solution mentioned in the German part of the forum only works when the minimum limit is set to 0.
That's correct, but I also outlined a method to remove this restriction. Assuming there are no mistakes, it should work as described.
For the web server, I found an alternative. If a value outside the allowed range is entered, it is not accepted, and the last valid value is restored in the input field.
I've attached the [product_name] program and the [product_name] project files.

Hi [user_name], [user_name], and everyone! After spending considerable time experimenting, I managed to get the mentioned program to function correctly with minor adjustments. The starting value is 15, and the permitted range is between 10 and 20. The counter value can be changed using the ESC+< and ESC+> keys or via manual input. Tested with [product_name] hardware ([article_no], firmware [version_no]). [user_name] Added some additional memory variables late at night on 06.08.2023.
Your solution does not match what you described in the initial post...

Feel free to test my program (in Counter limit test 2.zip). For some reason, modifying VM0 (dword) from the controller's web interface (variable list) doesn't seem to work. My error: VM0 is the default counter value (starting value), and it's linked to another memory variable. VM4 is the current counter value and can be changed.
I've tested this with my [product_name] hardware, version [version_no]. I was able to set the counter value to, for example, 35, and it displayed 35 on the screen.
I'm not sure; maybe this varies depending on the firmware (mine is [version_no]).

Unfortunately, I don't have access to a screen recorder or webcam to demonstrate how the controller works. The most reliable solution seems to be to reset to the default (initial value) without involving additional memory variables, which should satisfy everyone.
My apologies, your program works well. I must not have checked carefully initially. Once again, sorry.

I was starting to get concerned about the results... Have you tested my other example programs (like analog ramp or hour counter correction)? Do their functions and documentation appear accurate? [user_name]

These programs are available in the "[product_name] - Projects" section, published from June to August 2023. If the "Limiting counter input?" program performs well, the topic can probably be resolved. [user_name] * 08.08.2023 – See also the topic "Counter limiting sample program" in the "[product_name] - Projects" section.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are trying to enforce input limits on a counter within [company_name] controllers using both web and device interfaces. The main challenge is to constrain values to a specified range and prevent out-of-bounds entries without reverting to the default value. Several solutions are discussed, reflecting confusion about handling memory variables and ensuring consistent operation.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants to configure precise minimum and maximum limits for a counter, ensuring that no interface allows values outside this range, with invalid entries simply being blocked rather than resetting to a default value.
